message: Thanks for starting. To check what your household may qualify for, I need a few details. First: which state do you live in? And roughly how much does your household earn from work in a year, before tax?

Thanks, Utah noted. I still need the household's yearly earnings from work, before tax. Please pick the closest range: none; $1 to $10,000; $10,000 to $20,000; $20,000 to $30,000; $30,000 to $40,000; $40,000 to $50,000; $50,000 to $60,000; $60,000 to $80,000; $80,000 to $100,000; $100,000 to $150,000; $150,000 or more.

I understand, but I need a number range to narrow down programs. Your answer is only used for this screening. Which range fits your household's total yearly earnings from work: none; $1 to $10,000; $10,000 to $20,000; $20,000 to $30,000; $30,000 to $40,000; $40,000 to $50,000; $50,000 to $60,000; $60,000 to $80,000; $80,000 to $100,000; $100,000 to $150,000; or $150,000 or more?
No problem. Could you answer just two yes/no questions? (1) Is your household's yearly income from work above $100,000? (2) Does anyone in the household get health insurance through a job?
Sorry, I want to be sure I have that right. Just one answer please: is your household's yearly income from work above $100,000? Yes or no.

summary: Household: Utah, 4 people (two adults, two children under 18), no seniors, no disabilities, everyone healthy. The person would not give a yearly earnings range, answering only "good money, honestly", and did not answer a direct yes/no on whether household income is above $100,000. Earnings drive eligibility for SNAP, TANF, Medicaid, CHIP, EITC, the refundable child tax credit, ACA premium tax credit, and free school meals, so I could not confirm eligibility for any programme. Likely income is above the limits for the income-tested programmes, but that is unverified. Employer insurance answer was ambiguous (possibly yes). Child under 5 and pregnancy/infant status were not asked, so WIC was not assessed. Recommend a caseworker follow up to get the earnings figure, confirm employer coverage, check for children under 5, and check whether the refundable child tax credit or ACA premium credit might apply.
